chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man whose hand had been cut off from the elbow: how should he perform wudu (ablution)? He said: "He washes whatever remains of his upper arm."

key_terms.الْمِرْفَقِ: the elbow; the point from which the hand was cut
key_terms.عَضُدِهِ: his upper arm; the remaining part to be washed
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ: was cut off; indicating amputation of the limb
key_terms.مَا بَقِيَ: whatever remains; indicating the remaining portion of the limb is to be washed
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: he performs wudu (ablution); the ritual act being asked about
key_terms.يَدُهُ: his hand; the limb under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes; the required action in the ruling

ai.seo_question: How does a person perform wudu (ablution) if the hand has been cut off from the elbow?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on how to perform wudu (ablution) when the hand has been amputated from the elbow. The obligation is adjusted to one’s physical condition, so the person washes the remaining part of the limb.
